newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon parliament authorises $100 mln Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon parliament authorises $100 mln Eurobond.

text.p: Lebanon's parliament authorised the government on Thursday to issue a 10-year $100 million Eurobond to raise funds to rehabilitate Lebanon's power distribution stations and build new ones.
Parliament approved a government bill authorising the government to sign loan deals reaching to $265 million.

The Eurobond is part of a $1,290 million programme for improving the electricity network approved by parliament in 1995 but the government is required to obtain authorisation for each loan it takes out within the programme.

"The government is authorised to sign loan deals at the maximum value of $265 million and to issue $100 million Eurobonds to rehabilitate old and build new power distribution stations," the law approved on Thursday stated.
The eurobond will be issued by the government for the benefit of the Electricite du Liban state utility with a World Bank guarantee.
This issue will bring to $900 million the value of Eurobonds issued by the government since 1994.

Other loans approved in the package were $44.8 million from Indosuez Bank, $72.2 million from Paribas-France, $17 million from Compagnie Financiere de CIC et de L'Union Europeenne, $12.6 million from Germany's KFW (Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau), $4.7 million from Lebanon's Banque Saradar and $4.7 million from the World Bank.
